In the ablation table (Table 5), the **Transformer without pre-training averages 59.9**, and the **Transformer without the auxiliary LM objective has the highest average, 75.0** (Section 5, p. 7).

| Variant | Avg. Score |
|---|---|
| Transformer w/ aux LM (full) | 74.7 |
| Transformer w/o pre-training | 59.9 |
| Transformer w/o aux LM | **75.0** |
| LSTM w/ aux LM | 69.1 |

The highest average does not come from the full model, which scores 0.3 lower at 74.7 (p. 7). The paper explains this: the auxiliary objective "helps on the NLI tasks and QQP," and "larger datasets benefit from the auxiliary objective but smaller datasets do not" (p. 7).

The paper says that removing pre-training causes "a 14.8% decrease compared to our full model" (p. 7). This matches the gap between 74.7 and 59.9, which is 14.8 points, not a relative percentage.

The document marks only where sections start. Table 5 falls in Section 5, which begins on p. 7, so its exact page in the original PDF may differ.
